evals.prompt: We need an optional alarm setting in a shared CloudFormation fragment for one SEND component. Please implement it in the owning fragment and caller; existing callers must keep their current behavior.
evals.expected_output: Locates the authoritative fragment and all affected callers. Reuses the existing configuration path, gives an omitted optional parameter a type-valid default that preserves previous behavior and handles any sentinel explicitly. Changes only the caller that enables the capability, verifies omitted and populated behavior, and does not edit pn-configuration without authorization.
expectations: Identifies the owning fragment rather than editing a historical or generated copy.
Preserves deployment and behavior for callers that omit the new parameter.
Does not modify unrelated callers or pn-configuration.

evals.prompt: Review a pn-infra-confinfo Terraform change that adds an environment-specific value by editing generated terraform.tfvars directly, leaves codegen/pn-infra-configurations.yaml unchanged, and renames existing for_each keys as part of a cleanup. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Reports that the matrix is the source for environment values and that generated tfvars must be produced by user-run codegen, not hand-edited. Identifies the Terraform state-address risk of renaming for_each keys and distinguishes both confirmed issues from any unverified deployment impact. Makes no edits.
expectations: Points to the configuration matrix instead of treating generated tfvars as source.
Explains that renaming for_each keys changes Terraform resource identity.
Does not run codegen or edit pn-configuration.

evals.prompt: Review a new CONFINFO infrastructure monitoring feature that must notify a specific team through the warning route. The shared alarm fragment accepts a single AlarmSNSTopic, but the caller passes pn-AllAlarmSnsTopic instead of pn-WarningSnsTopic. The CORE topic permission and dispatcher routing configuration are not available in the supplied evidence. Do not modify anything.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the mismatch between the requested warning route and the caller's ordinary alarm topic. Recommends selecting the warning topic through the existing fragment parameter, not changing the fragment to publish to two topics. Traces CONFINFO-to-CORE publish permissions and the existing warning dispatcher's destination routing separately; requests missing evidence without declaring an unseen route or permission absent. Proposes a routing configuration change only if needed to reach the requested team, not a new dispatcher. Checks consistent AlarmActions and OKActions and keeps Slack routing out of the producer. Does not assume all infrastructure alarms belong on the warning route.
expectations: Identifies the incorrect topic passed by the caller against the explicit warning-routing requirement.
Uses the existing single-topic fragment interface and existing dispatcher rather than adding duplicate publication or a new dispatcher.
Checks cross-account publish permission and destination routing separately, treating unavailable evidence as a verification gap.
Makes no edits and does not generalize warning routing to every infrastructure alarm.

evals.prompt: We need two independent SEND consumers to receive every event. A proposal routes EventBridge to Queue A; one Lambda processes Queue A and a second relay Lambda also polls Queue A and copies each message into Queue B for the other consumer. Please assess the design before implementation.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the two Queue A pollers compete, so the relay and the first consumer will not each receive every event. Recommends independent EventBridge targets or another explicit fan-out into distinct queues if the producer contract and filters support it. Separates EventBridge delivery failures from processing failures and their DLQs. Does not claim that every queue-to-queue relay is inherently wrong.
expectations: Explains the competing-consumer defect on Queue A.
Proposes a concrete fan-out path that gives each responsibility its own queue.
Distinguishes routing DLQ from consumer-processing DLQs.

evals.prompt: A new SQS-triggered Lambda A synchronously invokes Lambda B for the same business operation, waits for completion, and ignores B's return value. B is also used elsewhere. Would you implement the direct invocation as proposed?
evals.expected_output: Treats direct Lambda-to-Lambda invocation for this relay as a SEND architectural anti-pattern by default. Checks responsibility, timeout, retries, duplicate effects, permissions and whether a response is actually needed. Proposes a shared library, an existing event contract, or an explicit asynchronous handoff when justified; a direct-call exception requires a concrete reason and user agreement. Does not invent a new queue without a concrete need or claim AWS forbids all direct invocations.
expectations: Identifies a concrete risk of synchronous coupling and retry interaction.
Evaluates whether B's shared responsibility justifies a separate component.
Challenges direct Lambda-to-Lambda invocation as the default design and requires a justified exception, without speculative infrastructure.

evals.prompt: Review a CloudFormation change that creates a persistent SEND DynamoDB table with DeletionPolicy: Retain but no UpdateReplacePolicy. The table has a fixed physical name, and a later key change may require replacement. Do not modify the template.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes stack deletion from update replacement and recommends UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain for the persistent table. Explains that retaining the old table does not migrate its data or allow a replacement table to reuse the same physical name while it still exists. Identifies the fixed-name replacement conflict without proposing explicit Delete as a shortcut. Makes no edits.
expectations: Identifies the missing UpdateReplacePolicy on the persistent table.
Explains replacement impact separately from stack deletion.
Identifies the fixed-name replacement conflict and explains that retention alone does not migrate data.

evals.prompt: Review a new Lambda Event Source Mapping on a SEND Kinesis stream. The requested behavior is to process new records after activation, but the change sets StartingPosition to TRIM_HORIZON, enables ReportBatchItemFailures while the handler only throws whole-batch errors, and has no stated retry or recovery policy. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Separates the starting-position decision from error-handling settings. Explains backlog and replay impact of TRIM_HORIZON versus LATEST and requests explicit approval before changing the mapping's position. Flags the mismatch between ReportBatchItemFailures and handler response, and asks how failed records are retried or recovered; considers IteratorAge monitoring without treating it as an error destination. Does not apply these stream rules to Firehose or SQS by analogy.
expectations: Identifies the TRIM_HORIZON/new-records conflict and the need for a user decision.
Identifies the unsupported partial-batch response setting.
Distinguishes retry/recovery from IteratorAge lag monitoring.

evals.prompt: Review a pn-infra output rename used by a SEND component deployment. The pn-cicd consumer still reads the old key in an accessible script; a second deployment path is not available in this workspace. This is review-only.
evals.expected_output: Traces the available consumer to file and line and reports the concrete impact of the mismatched output key. Gives compatible options: retain the old output, add a parallel key, or coordinate all consumers and release order. States exactly which second path cannot be verified and does not assert a defect there without evidence.
expectations: Cites the real consumer and explains the deployment consequence.
Provides a compatibility or coordinated-migration option.
Keeps the unavailable second path as a verification gap, not a confirmed defect.
Makes no edits.

evals.prompt: Implement a new configurable feature for a SEND component in dev only. The component repository contains the dev CloudFormation cfg and application environment-variable configuration. pn-configuration is also available and contains versions and configuration for higher environments, but no changes to those environments have been requested.
evals.expected_output: Locates the component's dev CloudFormation parameter file and application environment-variable configuration, traces which settings the feature needs, and changes only the relevant dev inputs and implementation. Keeps higher-environment versions and configuration in pn-configuration untouched unless explicitly requested. Considers future production behavior and identifies any later promotion needs without treating them as permission to perform that promotion. Follows the development workflow and its required decisions and approvals.
expectations: Identifies dev CloudFormation parameters and application environment-variable configuration in the component repository.
Updates only the dev configuration needed by the feature, without inventing unrelated settings.
Does not change higher-environment versions or configuration in pn-configuration without an explicit request.
Distinguishes planning for production from authorization to modify or deploy to it.

evals.prompt: A component exposes a new SEND API using the shared OpenAPI API Gateway fragment with IntendedUsage set. The team plans a component-only release and assumes that the intended usage tag automatically attaches the new API stage to its centralized Usage Plan. Review this assumption.
evals.expected_output: Explains that IntendedUsage/tagging is not itself proof of Usage Plan association. Traces the relevant pn-cicd Usage Plan update path, checks that the new API ID and unique stage are included in the release, and treats missing pipeline evidence as unverified rather than claiming the plan association occurred.
expectations: Distinguishes IntendedUsage from actual Usage Plan association.
Checks the component-only release path for the new API and unique stage.
Does not claim deployment success from template configuration alone.

evals.prompt: Design a CodeBuild project for a new SEND support feature. Another component has a similar build step but produces different artifacts and needs broader permissions. No suitable shared fragment has been identified yet. Should the resources live directly in the component's CloudFormation template, such as microservice.yml, or should we create a reusable fragment in pn-infra? Consider the same ownership and reuse decision for a resource such as an RDS database. Propose the design before implementation.
evals.expected_output: First checks adopted fragments and builders rather than assuming none exists. Compares a component-local definition with a new pn-infra fragment using concrete inputs, outputs, permissions, release coupling and ownership. Selects the owning template by resource lifecycle rather than always choosing microservice.yml. Recommends a new fragment only when a stable reusable responsibility is justified; shared definitions need not imply a shared physical resource or broader permissions. Applies the same reasoning to the RDS analogy without claiming a current RDS fragment is missing. Avoids speculative modes, unrelated caller migrations and infrastructure creation during design.
expectations: Checks existing fragments and builders before proposing a new reusable definition.
Compares component-local resources with a pn-infra fragment using real artifact and permission differences.
Chooses the owning template according to resource lifecycle rather than always using microservice.yml.
Distinguishes reusable definitions from shared physical instances and preserves separate permissions where needed.
Uses the RDS analogy without asserting that an existing fragment is absent, and avoids speculative generalization.

evals.prompt: A shared CloudFormation template is deployed in both CORE and CONFINFO. A change adds a String parameter for a CORE-only resource but gives it no Default, does not pass it from CONFINFO, and puts a Condition only on the resource. Review the proposed change without editing files.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the new parameter is required even when the conditional resource is not created, so the CONFINFO path can fail before evaluating that resource. If omission should preserve the old behavior, proposes Default: '' with explicit empty-value handling and verifies both deployment paths. If the value is truly required, identifies every caller that must supply it. Does not add a Rule merely to reassert missing-parameter validation.
expectations: Distinguishes parameter requiredness from resource Conditions.
Preserves the existing CONFINFO caller when the new behavior is CORE-only.
Does not add redundant CloudFormation validation.

evals.prompt: Review a Lambda with ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 10 and two SQS Event Source Mappings, each configured with ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency: 8. A proposed change increases both mapping limits and calls this harmless because the function has a cap. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the per-SQS-mapping maximum from the function-wide reserved concurrency. Notes that the two current mapping caps total 16, already above the reserved 10, and increasing them can worsen throttling; evaluates intended throughput, backlog, downstream protection and any other invocation sources before proposing consistent limits. Does not apply SQS ScalingConfig to Kinesis or DynamoDB Streams or claim that any cap alone guarantees successful processing.
expectations: Detects that the aggregate mapping cap exceeds the function reservation even before the proposed increase.
Explains the concrete throttling risk and the difference between the two limits.
Keeps the recommendation specific to SQS mappings and the actual processing demand.

evals.prompt: For the SEND Delivery informal API, a reviewer proposes a new CloudFormation Rule that only asserts InformalServiceApiPathOverrideV2 was supplied. Its parent parameter has no Default and is passed to a conditional nested API stack. The shared API fragment already has a Rule preventing both path overrides from being populated. Decide whether the new Rule adds useful validation, and explain where a Rule would be appropriate. Review only.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing mutual-exclusion Rule in the shared API fragment and identifies it as a real cross-parameter check. Explains that the parent parameter without Default is already required even when the nested stack Condition is false, so the proposed presence-only Rule is redundant. If the design should allow disabling the informal API without passing a path, proposes an optional empty default plus a conditional Rule requiring a nonempty path only when enabled, subject to caller compatibility. Checks actual cfg and pipeline inputs before claiming the current deployment is broken. Distinguishes Rules for parameter relationships, resource Conditions and parameter-level constraints.
expectations: Uses the actual shared-fragment mutual-exclusion Rule as the positive example.
Rejects the redundant presence-only Rule without declaring an unverified current bug.
Identifies the conditional enabled-path case in which a Rule could add value.
